transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with the weekly power-support meeting. We have four portable power units — P-1, P-2, P-3, and P-4 — all listed as serviceable and available. They need to go to the clinic, communications shelter, battery shop, and refrigerated storage area for the coming week. I'd like each of you to brief your area's needs so we can finalize the allocation and I can sign the support plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Ma'am, before we get into assignments, I need to flag something from yesterday's electrical inspection. P-2 is the only unit with the recently certified isolated-output transformer that the clinic's sensitive diagnostic equipment requires. The certification entry is still pending on the base inventory board, so it hasn't shown up there yet, but I personally confirmed it during the inspection. That means P-2 needs to go to the clinic.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ma'am, I need to flag something for the communications shelter. I confirmed this morning that the comm shelter's equipment requires regulated 28-volt output, which only P-4 provides. The updated compatibility note hasn't been added to the signal support annex yet, but I personally verified the requirement. So P-4 needs to go to the communications shelter.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Ma'am, I need to flag something for the battery shop. I confirmed with the battery-shop supervisor that their charging rack requires P-1's approved connector and grounding lead. The shop's revised power worksheet hasn't been forwarded to the base planning cell yet, so it wouldn't show up in their records, but I personally verified the requirement. That means P-1 needs to go to the battery shop.
transcript.speaker: A4

I confirmed that the refrigerated storage area will receive a continuous-temperature shipment requiring P-3's 24-hour runtime capability. The receiving manifest hasn't been linked to the power-allocation request yet, so it wouldn't appear in the planning records, but I personally verified the requirement. That means P-3 needs to go to the refrigerated storage area.
